messages:
sam: dropped an nsys trace from last night's dedicated job run. prepended a short summary below, full timeline attached to the build artifact link.
anika: thanks — quick question: is this the run after the quantization selector change on main? :thinking:
tj: yes, main@c4fd7ef. we rolled the new kernel selector heuristics that pick the 2-stage matmul for int8 by default.
sam: exact. symptoms: higher tail latency and weird CPU spikes pinned to the vLLM wrapper thread.
maria: can you paste the hot spots? even a tiny nsys excerpt helps.
sam: pasted the summary I pulled with nsys-ui -> summary -> top consumers (filtered to our pid):
```
CPU Time (ms)   Kernel/Function
120.3           vllm::Scheduler::dispatch_loop
73.8            trt::Engine::execute_async
28.1            trt::Engine::enqueue_binding
22.6            cudaMemcpyAsync
15.9            vllm::wrapper_spin_wait (user-space)
6.4             split_attention_kernel<int8>
5.1             gelu_fp32_kernel
```

```nsys profile: timeline shows execute_async blocks aligned with cuda events but huge gaps where wrapper thread spins waiting for completion before post-processing.
```
anika: wrapper_spin_wait is new — we added a short spin-before-sleep to reduce wakeups under low-latency configs. maybe it's mis-tuned.
tj: right, we tuned spin to 100us but I see it happening at 10-15ms frequently in trace.
maria: curious about batching. are we packing small sequences? kernel selection change might favor larger tiling that isn't efficient for short seqs.
sam: good call. batch histogram from the same run:
```
batch_size: 1 -> 42% (avg seq 24)
batch_size: 2 -> 28%
batch_size: 4 -> 18%
batch_size: 8+ -> 12%
```
sam: so most traffic is small batches; int8 2-stage matmul has higher fixed overhead but better throughput at larger sizes. for small batches execute_async overhead dominates.
tj: nailed it. also saw a regression in cuda-graph usage: we used to reuse graphs per (seq_len, batch) key; the new selector adds tiling meta so graph cache misses jumped ~3x.
perfbot: autometrics: graph_cache_hit_rate dropped 71% -> 24% after selector change. median p95 latency +18%.
sam: here's a perfetto slice showing graph capture vs execute events. byte offsets shortened for readability:
```
[0.000s] capture_graph(batch=2,seq=32) -> graph_id=0x7ff
[0.004s] trt::Engine::capture_kernel_config (15.2ms)
[0.020s] trt::Engine::instantiate_graph (12.1ms)
[0.035s] queue execute (exec 53ms)
[0.090s] vllm postprocess (18ms)
```
anika: capture time of 15ms is killer if it happens on cold path. should be offloaded to background thread or done lazily ahead-of-time.
maria: can we short-circuit capture when seq_len/batch combination is similar? maybe canonicalize tiling param.
tj: proposal: canonicalize to (ceil(seq/16)*16, nearest_power_of_two(batch)) for cache key. and fall back to quick path that uses previous kernel with a compatibility check.
sam: also need to tweak spin-wait: change to exponential backoff after 500us and yield thread after 2ms.
perfbot: regression alert created: PERF-2026. Link: https://perf.redwood/PRF-2026
deploy-bot: rolling a revert PR would impact weight 0.2 of traffic. ready to deploy if we approve.
anika: I'd prefer a targeted revert: keep kernel selector change but disable graph-key tiling change + spin-wait reversion. less blast radius.
maria: agree. steps:
1) disable tiling variation in selector (feature flag)
2) change spin policy to backoff + yield
3) add proactive graph prewarm for top 5 (batch,seq) combos observed in last 24h
4) backfill metrics for graph_cache_hit_rate per model

sam: implemented local patch for (2) and (3) and tested locally — p95 dropped ~12% in microbench.
tj: I'll open the PR with the feature-flag toggle and notes. tagging @anika for review.
anika: review done, leaving a comment about adding a unit test for cache key canonicalization.
maria: one more ask — instrument trs::Engine::execute_async to log enqueue vs execute micro-timings (just counters) so we can break down the 73ms bucket.
sam: added a small tracer: trt.enqueue_ns and trt.execute_ns counters. in last run enqueue ~9.8ms, execute ~61.2ms on avg.
tj: execute being 61ms for small batches is unexpected; could be kernel launch latency + int8 kernel poor occupancy. we should run a microbench on split_attention_kernel with seq 24 batch 1/2.
perfbot: scheduled microbench job: job/PRF-2026-microbench runs in 30m.
sam: thanks all. I'll attach the raw nsys and perfetto artifacts to the ticket and add the prewarm script.

-- end thread --
